q: Choose the correct tense: “They ____ married since 2005.”
why: 'Since' + a point in time takes the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “Look! The patient ____ up.”
why: 'Look!' signals an action happening now: present continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “She ____ tea every morning.”
why: A habitual action takes the simple present. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “By the time I reached the station, the train ____ already.”
why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “This time tomorrow, I ____ in a train to Mumbai.”
why: An action in progress at a future time takes the future continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “She said that she ____ the report the previous day.”
why: In reported speech a past time reference shifts to the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “It was the first time she ____ a surgery on her own.”
why: 'It was the first time' takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “I ____ him since he was a child.”
why: 'Since' with a past clause needs the present perfect; 'know' is a stative verb, not used in the continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “The professor, who ____ at this university since 1998, retires next month.”
why: 'Since 1998' up to now requires the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “I ____ you for ages; where have you been?”
why: 'For ages' (up to now) takes the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “I wish I ____ more attention in class last year.”
why: A wish about the past takes the past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “When we reached the cinema, the film ____ for ten minutes.”
why: Duration up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “Since the clinic ____ in 2012, it has treated thousands of patients.”
why: After 'since' the clause naming the starting point takes the simple past. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “It is two years since he ____ smoking.”
why: 'It is (time) since' is followed by the simple past. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct tense: “I ____ to Paris twice so far.”
why: 'So far' signals the present perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Either the nurse or the doctor ____ on duty tonight.”
why: With 'either...or' the verb agrees with the nearer subject (doctor, singular). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “My scissors ____ very sharp.”
why: 'Scissors' is a plural noun and takes a plural verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Ten kilometres ____ a long distance to walk.”
why: A distance considered as one unit takes a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “The police ____ investigating the case.”
why: 'Police' is always plural. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “A number of patients ____ waiting outside.”
why: 'A number of' takes a plural verb (unlike 'the number of'). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “She is one of those nurses who ____ always punctual.”
why: 'Who' refers to the plural 'nurses', so the verb is plural. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “He is the only one of the students who ____ passed.”
why: With 'the only one of', 'who' refers to 'one', so the verb is singular. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Every boy and every girl ____ been given a book.”
why: Subjects joined by 'and' but preceded by 'every' take a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “The flock of sheep ____ grazing on the hill.”
why: The head noun 'flock' is singular. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “The poet and philosopher ____ dead.”
why: One article for both nouns means one person, so the verb is singular. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Neither he nor I ____ to blame.”
why: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'I'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Not only the students but also the teacher ____ responsible.”
why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the teacher'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Many a student ____ failed in this examination.”
why: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “The news from the border ____ alarming.”
why: 'News' is singular in form and meaning. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Two-thirds of the work ____ completed.”
why: The verb agrees with the noun after 'of' (work, uncountable, singular). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “More than one candidate ____ failed the test.”
why: 'More than one' takes a singular noun and verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “She is ____ M.A. in English.”
why: 'M.A.' begins with the vowel sound /em/. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “____ sun rises in the east.”
why: Unique objects take 'the'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “I need ____ umbrella.”
why: 'Umbrella' starts with a vowel sound. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “I go to ____ bed at ten every night.”
why: 'Go to bed' (for sleep) uses no article. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “____ Himalayas are the highest mountain range in the world.”
why: Mountain ranges take 'the'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “Honesty is ____ best policy.”
why: Fixed proverb: 'the best policy'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “She wants to buy an unique gift for her mother’s birthday.”
why: 'Unique' begins with the consonant sound /j/, so 'a unique'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “She is working as ____ university lecturer.”
why: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /j/. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “He is a such brilliant student that everyone admires him.”
why: The order is 'such a' + adjective + noun: 'such a brilliant student'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “____ Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.”
why: Names of single mountains take no article. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “She has ____ little patience left, so she cannot wait.”
why: 'Little' without 'a' means hardly any (negative); 'a little' would mean some. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “He was ____ only person who knew the truth.”
why: 'Only' is a limiting word and takes 'the'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct article: “____ more you practise, ____ better you become.”
why: 'The ... the' with comparatives shows proportion. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “The shop remains closed ____ Sundays.”
why: 'On' is used with days of the week. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is married ____ my cousin.”
why: 'Married to' is the fixed form. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “We congratulated him ____ his success.”
why: 'Congratulate (someone) on'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is addicted ____ gambling.”
why: 'Addicted to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “The Collector is not satisfied ____ the progress of the work.”
why: 'Satisfied with'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “She is allergic ____ penicillin.”
why: 'Allergic to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “I am grateful ____ you for your timely help.”
why: 'Grateful to' a person, 'for' a thing. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “The train reaches Mumbai ____ the morning.”
why: 'In' is used with parts of the day (morning, afternoon, evening). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “The accused was convicted ____ murder.”
why: 'Convicted of' a crime. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “She insisted ____ paying the bill herself.”
why: 'Insist on'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is the legal heir ____ a large fortune.”
why: 'Heir to' a property or title. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “The workers were deprived ____ their wages.”
why: 'Deprive (someone) of'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “It is incumbent ____ every citizen to pay taxes.”
why: 'Incumbent on (or upon)'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “The manager is liable ____ any loss to the company.”
why: 'Liable for' a loss or damage. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “She is entitled ____ a pension after retirement.”
why: 'Entitled to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is averse ____ taking risks.”
why: 'Averse to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “Both the doctor ____ the nurse were present.”
why: Correlative pair: both ... and. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “Either you apologise ____ you leave the room.”
why: Correlative pair: either ... or. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “Not only did he fail the test, ____ he also lost the scholarship.”
why: Correlative pair: not only ... but also. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “No sooner had the bell rung ____ the students rushed out.”
why: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “No sooner had he reached the station when the train left.”
why: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than', not 'when'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “Take an umbrella lest it ____.”
why: 'Lest' is followed by 'should' + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “He studied day and night lest he will fail.”
why: 'Lest' takes 'should' (or the bare subjunctive), not 'will'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “I would rather die ____ beg for mercy.”
why: 'Would rather ... than'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “It was not until midnight ____ the fever subsided.”
why: Cleft structure: 'It was not until ... that'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct conjunction: “Not until the results were announced ____ he realise his mistake.”
why: After 'Not until' at the start, the auxiliary comes before the subject: 'did he realise'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Although he is rich, but he is not happy.”
why: 'Although' and 'but' must not be used together. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Hardly had she entered the room than the lights went out.”
why: 'Hardly' pairs with 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “You ought ____ respect your elders.”
why: 'Ought' is followed by 'to' + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct modal: “He ____ to play cricket every evening, but now he doesn’t.”
why: 'Used to' expresses a past habit that no longer exists. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “He needs not go there today.”
why: As a modal, 'need' takes no -s: 'He need not go' (or 'does not need to go'). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct modal: “She dare not ____ the Principal.”
why: The modal 'dare' is followed by the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “I would rather ____ at home than go out in this rain.”
why: 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “May God ____ you with a long life!”
why: 'May' expressing a wish takes the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “She used to ____ up at five every morning.”
why: 'Used to' (past habit) is followed by the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “He is used to ____ up at five every morning.”
why: 'Be used to' (accustomed to) takes a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “Need I ____ the form again?”
why: The modal 'need' in a question takes the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Fill in the blank: “It is essential that he ____ present at the meeting.”
why: After 'it is essential that', the subjunctive (bare infinitive) is used. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct modal: “He ____ have stolen the money; he was out of town that day.”
why: 'Cannot have' + past participle expresses certainty that something did not happen. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct modal: “You ____ have bought the medicine; we already had it.”
why: 'Needn't have' + past participle means an action done but unnecessary. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct modal: “____ you please lend me your pen?”
why: 'Could' is used for a polite request. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “The news about the floods were shocking to everyone.”
why: 'News' is singular, so 'was' is needed. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “She prefers tea than coffee.”
why: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Every boys in the class has a textbook.”
why: 'Every' takes a singular noun: 'Every boy'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Despite of the heavy rain, the match continued.”
why: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'; 'in spite of' or 'despite'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “I look forward to meet you at the conference next week.”
why: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund: 'to meeting'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Scarcely had the lecture ended than the students left the hall.”
why: 'Scarcely/Hardly' pairs with 'when', not 'than'. Like GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

q: Identify the error: “The police has arrested the two suspects from the market.”
why: 'Police' is a plural noun, so 'have arrested'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Little did he realised the danger until it was too late.”
why: After 'did' the main verb is in the base form: 'realise'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “The scissors is lying on the table near the lamp.”
why: 'Scissors' is a plural-only noun: 'are lying'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “She is one of the best doctors who has served in this hospital.”
why: In 'one of the ... who', the relative pronoun refers to the plural 'doctors': 'have served'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “The man, whom everyone thought was honest, cheated them.”
why: 'Who' is the subject of 'was honest'; 'everyone thought' is parenthetical. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “Not only he is a good doctor but also a kind human being.”
why: 'Not only' at the start requires inversion: 'Not only is he'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “The secret must remain between you and I.”
why: A preposition takes the objective case: 'between you and me'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the error: “The criteria for selection is very strict.”
why: 'Criteria' is the plural of 'criterion': 'are'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “He don’t like spicy food.”
why: Third person singular present negative takes 'doesn’t' + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “She is married with a surgeon.”
opts: She is married by a surgeon.
She is married for a surgeon.
She is married from a surgeon.
She is married to a surgeon.
why: 'Married to' is the correct collocation. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “I am living in Panaji since 2010.”
opts: I am living in Panaji from 2010.
I was living in Panaji since 2010.
I have been living in Panaji since 2010.
why: 'Since' with a point in time takes the present perfect (continuous). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “He insisted to go there alone.”
opts: He insisted on going there alone.
He insisted to going there alone.
He insisted for go there alone.
He insisted on to go there alone.
why: 'Insist on' is followed by a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “I prefer walking than driving to work.”
opts: I prefer walking to driving to work.
I prefer walking than to drive to work.
I prefer to walk than driving to work.
I prefer walk to drive to work.
why: 'Prefer X to Y' with matching forms; 'than' is not used. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “She was too tired that she could not walk.”
opts: She was such tired that she could not walk.
She was too tired to she could not walk.
She was so tired as she could not walk.
She was so tired that she could not walk.
why: 'So ... that' expresses result; 'too' needs 'to + verb'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “The patient was operated by Dr Rao yesterday.”
opts: The patient was operated at by Dr Rao yesterday.
The patient was operated of by Dr Rao yesterday.
The patient was operated on by Dr Rao yesterday.
The patient was operating by Dr Rao yesterday.
why: The prepositional verb 'operate on' keeps its preposition in the passive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “I cannot help to laugh at his jokes.”
opts: I cannot help laugh at his jokes.
I cannot but laughing at his jokes.
I cannot helping laugh at his jokes.
I cannot help laughing at his jokes.
why: 'Cannot help' is followed by a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “Walking down the corridor, the lights suddenly went off.”
opts: As I was walking down the corridor, the lights suddenly went off.
While walking down the corridor, the lights suddenly went off.
Walking down the corridor, suddenly the lights went off.
The lights suddenly went off, walking down the corridor.
why: The participial phrase dangles; only the clause with its own subject is correct. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “Many a patient have recovered after this treatment.”
opts: Many a patients has recovered after this treatment.
Many a patient has recovered after this treatment.
Many a patients have recovered after this treatment.
Many patient has recovered after this treatment.
why: 'Many a' takes a singular noun and a singular verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “He is the man whom I think is responsible for the leak.”
opts: He is the man whom I think he is responsible for the leak.
He is the man who I think he is responsible for the leak.
He is the man who I think is responsible for the leak.
He is the man who I think are responsible for the leak.
why: 'Who' is the subject of 'is responsible'; 'I think' is parenthetical. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “Let you and I settle this matter at once.”
opts: Let you and me to settle this matter at once.
Let you and I to settle this matter at once.
Let you and me settled this matter at once.
Let you and me settle this matter at once.
why: 'Let' takes the objective case and a bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct version: “The reason is because he was ill.”
opts: The reason is that he was ill.
The reason is for he was ill.
The reason is why he was ill.
The reason is due to that he was ill.
why: 'The reason is' is followed by a 'that' clause, not 'because'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct inversion of: “He seldom goes to the cinema.”
opts: Seldom he goes to the cinema.
Seldom does he go to the cinema.
Seldom does he goes to the cinema.
Seldom goes he to the cinema.
why: Negative adverb first, then 'does' + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Complete with the correct inversion: “Never again ____ such a mistake.”
why: 'Never' at the start is followed by auxiliary + subject + verb. Like GPSC CBRT, Mar 2026.

q: Choose the correct option: “No sooner had the surgeon entered the theatre ____ the lights failed.”
why: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Complete the sentence: “Not until the report arrived ____ the matter.”
why: 'Not until' + clause is followed by inversion in the main clause. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Complete the sentence: “Under no circumstances ____ the ward after 9 p.m.”
why: A negative phrase in front position requires modal + subject. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct inversion: “Not only ...”
opts: Not only he arrived late, but he also forgot the files.
Not only did he arrived late, but he also forgot the files.
Not only arrived he late, but he also forgot the files.
Not only did he arrive late, but he also forgot the files.
why: 'Not only' + did + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct inversion of: “If I had known about the problem, I would have helped you.”
opts: Had I known about the problem, I would have helped you.
Have I known about the problem, I would have helped you.
Did I know about the problem, I would have helped you.
Were I known about the problem, I would have helped you.
why: Third conditional inverts to 'Had + subject + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct inversion of: “If you need any help, please call me.”
opts: Would you need any help, please call me.
Should you need any help, please call me.
Shall you need any help, please call me.
Were you need any help, please call me.
why: First-conditional inversion uses 'Should + subject + base verb'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Complete the sentence: “Not a single word ____ during the interview.”
why: Negative object phrase in front requires did + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Complete the sentence: “Seldom ____ such a rare disease been reported in this district.”
why: Seldom + has + singular subject + past participle (present perfect passive). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct inversion of: “The accident was so terrible that the road remained closed for hours.”
opts: So terrible was the accident that the road remained closed for hours.
So terrible the accident was that the road remained closed for hours.
Such terrible was the accident that the road remained closed for hours.
So terrible did the accident was that the road remained closed for hours.
why: 'So + adjective' in front position inverts the verb 'be' and the subject. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct inversion of: “If he were to apologise, I would forgive him.”
opts: Be he to apologise, I would forgive him.
Were he to apologise, I would forgive him.
Did he to apologise, I would forgive him.
Should he were to apologise, I would forgive him.
why: 'If ... were to' is inverted as 'Were + subject + to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Complete the sentence: “Nowhere in the report ____ any mention of side effects.”
why: Negative adverbial in front: verb 'be' precedes 'there'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If you heat water to 100°C, it ____.”
why: Zero conditional: present simple in both clauses for general truths. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If he works hard, he ____ the examination.”
why: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If I ____ a bird, I would fly to you.”
why: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons in the if-clause. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “I would have attended the seminar if I ____ about it earlier.”
why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Unless you ____ the rules, you will be fined.”
why: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the verb stays affirmative. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “I will lend you the book provided that you ____ it by Monday.”
why: 'Provided that' takes the present tense for future reference. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Take an umbrella in case it ____ this evening.”
why: 'In case' is followed by the present simple for future time. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If she had taken the medicine on time, she ____ better now.”
why: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Had the ambulance arrived earlier, the child ____.”
why: Inverted third conditional takes 'would have + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the grammatically incorrect conditional sentence:
opts: If she would have studied, she would have passed.
If I had known, I would have told you.
If he comes, I will go with him.
If I were rich, I would travel.
why: 'Would have' is not used in the if-clause: 'If she had studied'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If it had not been for your help last year, I ____ in that examination.”
why: Third conditional for an unreal past situation. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If he had listened to the doctor then, he ____ in hospital now.”
why: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “She would have recovered sooner had she ____ the prescribed diet.”
why: 'Had she + past participle' is the inverted third conditional. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “But for your timely help last night, the patient ____.”
why: 'But for' + past reference takes 'would have + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “If I weren’t so busy these days, I ____ the conference last week.”
why: Mixed conditional: present state, past result. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: The patient said, “My head aches.”
opts: The patient said that my head ached.
The patient said that his head would ache.
The patient said that his head ached.
The patient said that his head had been ached.
why: Present simple backshifts to past simple; 'my' becomes 'his'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: The boy said, “I have finished my homework.”
opts: The boy said that he has finished his homework.
The boy said that I had finished my homework.
The boy said that he finished his homework.
The boy said that he had finished his homework.
why: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect; pronouns change. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said to me, “Thank you.”
why: 'Thank you' is reported with the verb 'thanked' + object. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “I saw her yesterday.”
opts: He said that he saw her yesterday.
He said that he had seen her the day before.
He said that he had seen her yesterday.
He says that he had seen her the day before.
why: Past simple becomes past perfect; 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: The nurse said to the patient, “Have you taken your tablets?”
opts: The nurse asked the patient if he has taken his tablets.
The nurse asked the patient that had he taken his tablets.
The nurse asked the patient whether he had taken his tablets.
The nurse asked the patient whether had he taken his tablets.
why: Yes/no questions use 'if/whether' with statement word order and backshift. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: The teacher said to the students, “Do not make noise.”
opts: The teacher said the students do not make noise.
The teacher told the students do not make noise.
The teacher told the students to not made noise.
The teacher told the students not to make noise.
why: A negative command is reported with 'told ... not to + verb'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into direct speech: He asked her whether she would attend the meeting.
opts: He said to her, “Will you attend the meeting?”
He said to her, “Did you attend the meeting?”
He said to her, “Are you attending the meeting?”
He said to her, “Whether will you attend the meeting?”
why: 'Would' in reported speech returns to 'will'; question order is restored. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: “Hurrah! We have won the match,” said the boys.
opts: The boys said with joy that they have won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
The boys exclaimed that we had won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy they won the match.
why: Exclamations use 'exclaimed with joy that'; present perfect becomes past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: The doctor said to me, “You should not skip meals.”
opts: The doctor said me not to skip meals.
The doctor advised me that not skip meals.
The doctor advised me not to skip meals.
The doctor told me should not skip meals.
why: 'Should' advice is reported with 'advised ... (not) to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said to me, “You ought to see a doctor.”
opts: He told me that you ought to see a doctor.
He told me that I had ought to see a doctor.
He told that I ought to see a doctor.
He told me that I ought to see a doctor.
why: 'Ought to' does not change; the pronoun 'you' becomes 'I'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “If I had known, I would have come.”
opts: He said that if he had known, he would have come.
He said that if he has known, he would come.
He said that if he had had known, he would have come.
He said that if he knew, he would have come.
why: A third conditional is already in the past perfect and does not change. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: She said, “I used to play tennis.”
opts: She said that she had used to play tennis.
She said that she used to play tennis.
She said that she has used to play tennis.
She said that she would used to play tennis.
why: 'Used to' does not backshift. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: He will say, “I am busy.”
opts: He will say that he was busy.
He will say that he had been busy.
He will say that he is busy.
He will say that he would be busy.
why: When the reporting verb is in the future tense, there is no backshift. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said to me, “I am leaving now; will you join me?”
opts: He told me that he is leaving now and asked if I would join him.
He told me that he was leaving then and asked whether I will join him.
He said me that he was leaving then and asked would I join him.
He told me that he was leaving then and asked if I would join him.
why: Mixed sentences use 'told' for the statement and 'asked if' for the question; 'now' becomes 'then'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into direct speech: The patient asked the doctor whether he could go home that day.
opts: The patient said to the doctor, “Can I go home today?”
The patient said to the doctor, “Can he go home today?”
The patient said to the doctor, “Can I go home that day?”
The patient said to the doctor, “May I go home yesterday?”
why: 'Could' returns to 'can', 'that day' returns to 'today', and the question order is restored. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The cook prepares the meal every day.”
opts: The meal was prepared by the cook every day.
The meal is prepared by the cook every day.
The meal is preparing by the cook every day.
The meal prepared by the cook every day.
why: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “She sang a beautiful song.”
opts: A beautiful song was sang by her.
A beautiful song is sung by her.
A beautiful song was sung by her.
A beautiful song has been sung by her.
why: Past simple passive: was + past participle ('sung'). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct active voice: “The thief was caught by the police.”
opts: The police had caught the thief.
The police was catching the thief.
why: Past simple passive converts to past simple active. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “They are building a new hospital.”
opts: A new hospital is being built by them.
A new hospital is built by them.
A new hospital has been built by them.
A new hospital was being built by them.
why: Present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The clerk has not filed the application.”
opts: The application was not filed by the clerk.
The application has not been filed by the clerk.
The application is not being filed by the clerk.
The application has not filed by the clerk.
why: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “You should not ignore these symptoms.”
opts: These symptoms should not been ignored.
These symptoms should not be ignored.
These symptoms should not being ignored.
why: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Where did you buy this book?”
opts: Where this book was bought by you?
Where is this book bought by you?
Where did this book bought by you?
Where was this book bought by you?
why: Past simple question becomes 'was + subject + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “People once believed that the earth was flat.”
opts: The earth was once believed to be flat.
The earth is once believed to be flat.
The earth once believed to be flat.
The earth was once believed being flat.
why: Past 'believed' becomes 'was believed' with an infinitive. Like GPSC CBRT, May 2026.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Do not touch the wires.”
opts: Let not the wires be touched.
The wires are not to touch.
Let not the wires being touched.
why: Negative imperative passive: Let not + object + be + past participle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The principal gave the students certificates.”
opts: The students gave certificates by the principal.
The principal was given certificates to the students.
The students were given certificates by the principal.
Certificates are given the students by the principal.
why: With two objects, either can become the subject; the others misuse tense or roles. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “I saw him enter the room.”
opts: He was seen enter the room by me.
He was seen to entered the room by me.
He saw to enter the room by me.
He was seen to enter the room by me.
why: A bare infinitive after a perception verb becomes a to-infinitive in the passive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Nobody can solve this problem.”
opts: This problem cannot be solved by anyone.
This problem can not be solved by nobody.
This problem could not be solved by anyone.
This problem is not solved by anyone.
why: Negative subject becomes 'cannot be + past participle ... by anyone'; avoid double negatives. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive form: “I don’t like people laughing at me.”
opts: I don’t like being laughing at.
I don’t like being laughed at.
I don’t like be laughed at.
why: After 'like' the passive gerund is 'being + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct passive form: “He wants someone to repair the clinic roof.”
opts: He wants the clinic roof being repaired.
He wants the clinic roof to repair.
He wants the clinic roof to be repaired.
He is wanted the clinic roof repaired.
why: The passive infinitive is 'to be + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “rapid”:
why: 'Rapid' means moving at great speed, as does 'swift'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “hasten”:
why: To hasten is to hurry or speed up. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “genuine”:
why: 'Genuine' means real or authentic. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “copious”:
why: 'Copious' means abundant; 'ample' is closest. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “placate”:
why: To placate is to calm or appease someone. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “reticent”:
why: 'Reticent' means unwilling to speak freely; reserved. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “magnanimous”:
why: 'Magnanimous' means generous and forgiving, especially towards a rival. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “mitigate”:
why: To mitigate is to make less severe; alleviate. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “pernicious”:
why: 'Pernicious' means having a gradual, destructive effect; harmful. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “capricious”:
why: 'Capricious' means given to sudden changes of mood or behaviour; fickle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “cogent”:
why: A cogent argument is clear, logical and convincing. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “ostensible”:
why: 'Ostensible' means seeming or outwardly stated, though perhaps not real. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “inexorable”:
why: 'Inexorable' means impossible to stop or persuade; relentless. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “sycophant”:
why: A sycophant is a person who flatters the powerful for advantage. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “perfunctory”:
why: 'Perfunctory' means done with minimal effort; cursory. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “recalcitrant”:
why: 'Recalcitrant' means stubbornly resisting authority; obstinate. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “equivocal”:
why: 'Equivocal' means open to more than one interpretation; ambiguous. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “laconic”:
why: 'Laconic' means using very few words; terse. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “ancient”:
why: 'Ancient' means very old; its opposite is 'modern'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “generous”:
why: A generous person gives freely; a miserly one hoards. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “expand”:
why: To expand is to enlarge; to contract is to shrink. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “diligent”:
why: 'Diligent' means hardworking; 'indolent' means lazy. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “verbose”:
why: 'Verbose' means using too many words; 'succinct' means briefly expressed. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “zenith”:
why: 'Zenith' is the highest point; 'nadir' is the lowest point. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “lucid”:
why: 'Lucid' means clear and easily understood; 'obscure' means unclear. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “prudent”:
why: 'Prudent' means careful and sensible; 'reckless' means heedless of danger. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “garrulous”:
why: 'Garrulous' means excessively talkative; 'taciturn' means habitually silent. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “benign”:
why: 'Benign' means gentle or harmless; 'malignant' means harmful or evil in intent. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “gregarious”:
why: 'Gregarious' means fond of company; 'reclusive' means avoiding company. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “munificent”:
why: 'Munificent' means very generous; 'parsimonious' means extremely stingy. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “pragmatic”:
why: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things realistically; 'idealistic' is the opposite. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “ebullient”:
why: 'Ebullient' means cheerful and full of energy; 'dejected' means low in spirits. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “sporadic”:
why: 'Sporadic' means occurring at irregular intervals; 'constant' means continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “extol”:
why: To extol is to praise highly; to denigrate is to belittle. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “A person who speaks many languages”
why: A polyglot is a person who knows and uses several languages. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “Government by the people”
why: Democracy is rule by the people, directly or through elected representatives. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “A person who hates mankind”
why: A misanthrope dislikes and distrusts people in general. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “Able to use both hands equally well”
why: Ambidextrous means equally skilled with the right and left hand. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “The study of the origin and history of words”
why: Etymology traces the origin and development of words. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “A person who is gradually recovering health after illness”
why: A convalescent is someone regaining health after sickness. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “A person who walks in sleep”
why: A somnambulist is a sleepwalker. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “A disease regularly found among people in a particular area”
why: An endemic disease is constantly present in a particular region or population. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “Government by a small group of people”
why: Oligarchy is rule by a few persons. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the one word for: “A person who bears pain and hardship without showing feelings”
why: A stoic endures suffering with calm self-control. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to break the ice”:
opts: to start a conversation in an awkward social situation
why: 'Break the ice' means to ease initial tension among strangers. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a piece of cake”:
why: 'A piece of cake' means something very easy. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “under the weather”:
why: 'Under the weather' means feeling slightly ill. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to cost an arm and a leg”:
why: The idiom means to be very costly. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to bite the bullet”:
opts: to face a painful situation with courage
why: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure something unpleasant bravely. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to beat around the bush”:
opts: to avoid coming to the point
why: The idiom means to talk without addressing the main issue. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “the last straw”:
opts: the final event that makes a situation unbearable
why: From 'the straw that broke the camel's back'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a white elephant”:
opts: a costly possession that is of little use
why: A white elephant is expensive to maintain but useless. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “Achilles' heel”:
why: Achilles' heel is a weak spot in an otherwise strong person. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a Pyrrhic victory”:
opts: a victory won at too great a cost
why: After King Pyrrhus, whose victory cost him most of his army. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to carry coals to Newcastle”:
why: Newcastle was a coal-producing town, so supplying coal there is pointless. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to eat humble pie”:
opts: to apologise humbly and admit one's error
why: The idiom means to accept humiliation after being proved wrong. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “Hobson's choice”:
opts: an apparent choice where there is really no alternative
why: Named after Thomas Hobson: take what is offered or nothing. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a swan song”:
opts: a final performance or achievement before retirement
why: A swan song is a last appearance or work. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The surgeon decided to ____ the operation until the patient was stable.”
why: 'Put off' means to postpone. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “Please ____ the document carefully before signing it.”
why: 'Look through' means to examine. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “She ____ the job offer because the salary was too low.”
why: 'Turn down' means to reject. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The patient's fever has not ____ even after three days.”
why: 'Come down' means to decrease, as of a fever. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The issue of staff shortage was ____ at the board meeting.”
why: 'Bring up' means to raise a topic. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “She ____ her mother in looks and manner.”
why: 'Take after' means to resemble a parent or relative. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The negotiators managed to ____ their differences before the deadline.”
why: 'Iron out' means to settle problems or disagreements. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “He tried to ____ his negligence as bad luck.”
why: 'Pass off as' means to represent falsely as something else. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The students were told to ____ before the examination.”
why: 'Buckle down' means to start working seriously. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The new health policy will ____ rural clinics positively.”
why: 'Affect' is a verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is mostly a noun. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The ____ of the medical college addressed the new students.”
why: 'Principal' means head; 'principle' means a rule or belief. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The red scarf was a perfect ____ to her white dress.”
why: 'Complement' means something that completes; 'compliment' means praise. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The police tried to ____ a confession from the suspect.”
why: 'Elicit' means to draw out; 'illicit' means unlawful. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The clerk ordered pens, files and other office ____.”
why: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' means not moving. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The lawyer gave the family sound ____ on the matter.”
why: 'Counsel' means advice; 'council' means an administrative body. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The doctor tried to ____ the anxious parents that the child was safe.”
why: 'Assure' is used with a person; 'ensure' means to make certain. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The ____ surgeon was honoured with a national award.”
why: 'Eminent' means distinguished; 'imminent' means about to happen. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The committee needs a ____ arbiter who has no stake in the outcome.”
why: 'Disinterested' means impartial; 'uninterested' means bored. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: The word has double c and double m. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: One c and two s's: necessary. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: Double c, double r, and ends in -ence. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: Spelt con-sci-en-tious. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: Silent p: pneu-mo-nia. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: Double l and double n. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: The only English word ending in -sede (with no other -cede form). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: Spelt idiosyncrasy. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Find the correctly spelt word:
why: Ends in -ible: irresistible. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “She spoke so softly that nobody could hear her,” the clause “that nobody could hear her” is a:
why: 'So ... that' introduces an adverb clause of result. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “The book that you lent me is interesting,” the clause “that you lent me” is a:
why: It qualifies the noun 'book', so it is an adjective clause. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “Wherever you go, I will follow you,” the clause “Wherever you go” is a:
why: 'Wherever' shows place and modifies the verb 'follow'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “The fact that he had lied upset everyone,” the clause “that he had lied” is a:
why: The clause explains the noun 'fact' and acts as a noun in apposition. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “She is the doctor whose advice saved my father,” the clause “whose advice saved my father” is a:
why: 'Whose' is a relative pronoun; the clause qualifies 'doctor'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “He behaved as if he owned the place,” the clause “as if he owned the place” is a:
why: 'As if' introduces an adverb clause of manner. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “Hard as he tried, he could not lift the stone,” the clause “Hard as he tried” is a:
why: 'Hard as he tried' means 'though he tried hard': concession. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “Unless you work hard, you will fail,” the clause “Unless you work hard” is a:
why: 'Unless' means 'if not' and introduces a condition. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the principal clause in: “When the bell rang, the students left the hall.”
opts: left the hall when the bell rang
why: The principal clause makes complete sense on its own; 'When the bell rang' is subordinate. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Which sentence contains an adjective clause?
opts: I know the place where he lives.
why: In the key, 'where he lives' qualifies the noun 'place'; in the others the clause is a noun or adverb clause. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In the sentence “The day when we met was memorable,” the clause “when we met” is a:
why: 'When' here is a relative adverb qualifying the noun 'day'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of the word “beautifully”: “She sings beautifully.”
why: It modifies the verb 'sings'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “Alas” in: “Alas! The patient could not be saved.”
why: 'Alas' expresses sudden emotion. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “after” in: “The patient was shifted to the ward after the operation.”
why: It is followed by the noun phrase 'the operation'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “after” in: “She left after the meeting had ended.”
why: It joins the clause 'the meeting had ended' to the main clause. GPSC-style practice item.

q: In “The poor need our help,” the word “poor” functions as a:
why: After 'the', it names a class of people, so it works as a noun. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “book” in: “Please book a table for dinner.”
why: It is the action word of the sentence. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “only” in: “He is the only candidate who passed.”
why: It modifies the noun 'candidate'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “Neither” in: “Neither of the answers is correct.”
why: It stands for a noun and is followed by 'of'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “yet” in: “It was raining, yet we went out.”
why: It joins two clauses and shows contrast. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Identify the part of speech of “since” in: “She has not called since.”
why: It has no object or clause following, so it is an adverb meaning 'from then till now'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “You are a doctor, ____?”
why: Positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “I am late, ____?”
why: 'I am' takes the tag 'aren’t I'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “Nobody called, ____?”
why: 'Nobody' is negative, so the tag is positive; it takes 'they'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “Open the door, ____?”
why: An imperative takes 'will you' as its tag. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “There is hardly any water left, ____?”
why: 'Hardly' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “He used to live here, ____?”
why: 'Used to' is past, so the tag uses 'did'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “Everyone has submitted the form, ____?”
why: 'Everyone' takes the plural pronoun 'they' in a tag. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “Don’t be late, ____?”
why: A negative imperative takes 'will you'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct question tag: “You have never been to Goa, ____?”
why: 'Never' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “She enjoys ____ novels.”
why: 'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “He decided ____ the job.”
why: 'Decide' is followed by an infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “He avoided ____ the question.”
why: 'Avoid' is followed by a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “I look forward to ____ you next week.”
why: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so a gerund follows. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “She promised ____ on time.”
why: 'Promise' is followed by an infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “I remember ____ the letter yesterday; I posted it myself.”
why: 'Remember' + gerund refers to a past act recalled. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Don’t forget ____ the register before you leave.”
why: 'Forget' + infinitive refers to a duty not yet done. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “He is used to ____ up early.”
why: 'Be used to' takes a gerund (to is a preposition). GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “It is no use ____ over spilt milk.”
why: 'It is no use' is followed by a gerund. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “She suggested ____ the meeting.”
why: 'Suggest' takes a gerund, not an infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Rina is the ____ girl in her class.” (tall)
why: Superlative of a short adjective takes -est. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Of the two medicines, this one is the ____.”
why: Two items are compared, so the comparative 'better' is used. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Of the two sisters, Rita is the ____.” (intelligent)
why: Two persons: comparative; long adjectives take 'more'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The population of Goa is smaller than ____ of Maharashtra.”
why: 'That' replaces the singular noun 'population' to avoid repetition. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “She is two years ____ than her cousin.”
why: 'Than' follows 'older'; 'elder' is not used with 'than'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “For ____ details, please contact the office.”
why: 'Further' means additional; 'farther' refers to distance. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct form: “Everest is the ____ peak in the world.”
why: Superlative of 'high' is 'highest'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “____ is knocking at the door?”
why: 'Who' is the subject of 'is knocking'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “To ____ did you give the prescription?”
why: 'Whom' is the object of the preposition 'to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The man ____ car was stolen lodged a complaint.”
why: 'Whose' shows possession. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “Between you and ____, the plan is risky.”
why: A preposition takes the object form 'me'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “All ____ glitters is not gold.”
why: After 'all', the relative pronoun 'that' is used. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “The candidate ____ I believe is the best has been selected.”
why: 'Who' is the subject of 'is'; 'I believe' is parenthetical. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “He prided ____ on his punctuality.”
why: 'Pride' is followed by a reflexive pronoun. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “He failed the exam, ____ surprised nobody.”
why: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'that' cannot follow a comma. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “I have two pens; one is blue and ____ is black.”
why: With two items, the remaining one is 'the other'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct word: “It is the best film ____ I have ever seen.”
why: After a superlative, 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: What a beautiful day, it is.
What a beautiful day it is,
What a beautiful day it is!
What a beautiful day it is?
why: An exclamatory sentence ends with an exclamation mark. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: Mumbai, Delhi and, Chennai are big cities.
Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai are big cities.
Mumbai Delhi, and Chennai are big cities.
Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai, are big cities.
why: Commas separate items in a list; none separates subject and verb. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: The children’s ward is on the first floor.
The childrens ward is on the first floor.
The childrens’ ward is on the first floor.
The children’s’ ward is on the first floor.
why: 'Children' is an irregular plural, so the possessive is 'children’s'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: He said, I will come tomorrow.”
why: A comma introduces the direct speech, which is enclosed in quotation marks. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: He was tired; however, he continued working.
He was tired; however he, continued working.
He was tired, however, he continued working.
He was tired however; he continued working.
why: A semicolon precedes the conjunctive adverb 'however', followed by a comma. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: You will need the following; a pen, a ruler and a pencil.
You will need, the following: a pen, a ruler and a pencil.
You will need the following, a pen, a ruler and a pencil.
You will need the following: a pen, a ruler and a pencil.
why: A colon introduces a list after a complete clause. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: My brother who is a surgeon, lives in Pune.
My brother, who is a surgeon; lives in Pune.
My brother, who is a surgeon, lives in Pune.
My brother, who is a surgeon lives in Pune.
why: A non-defining clause is enclosed by a pair of commas. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
why: The question mark stays inside the quotes and no comma follows it. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence:
opts: She is a twenty-five year-old surgeon.
She is a twenty five year old surgeon.
She is a twenty five-year old surgeon.
why: A compound modifier before a noun is hyphenated throughout. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Which of the following is a simple sentence?
opts: Being ill, he stayed at home.
Though he was ill, he came.
He stayed at home because he was ill.
why: It has one finite verb and one clause; the others are complex or compound. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Which of the following is a compound sentence?
opts: She said that she was ill.
I called him, but he did not answer.
why: Two independent clauses are joined by 'but'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct transformation: “He is so weak that he cannot walk.”
opts: He is so weak to walk.
He is weak enough to walk.
He is too weak to walk.
He is very weak to walk.
why: 'So ... that ... not' becomes 'too ... to'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into a simple sentence: “As soon as he saw the police, he ran away.”
opts: On seeing the police, he ran away.
After see the police, he ran away.
At seeing the police, he ran away.
By seeing the police, he ran away.
why: 'As soon as' is expressed as 'On + -ing'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into a complex sentence: “Work hard, or you will fail.”
opts: If you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
If you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will not fail.
why: 'Or' (otherwise) becomes 'if ... not'; 'unless' already carries negation. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into a compound sentence: “Though he is poor, he is honest.”
opts: He is poor, so he is honest.
He is poor, but he is honest.
He is poor, for he is honest.
He is poor, or he is honest.
why: 'Though' (concession) becomes 'but'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into a complex sentence: “Having finished the work, he went home.”
opts: Before he had finished the work, he went home.
Although he finished the work, he went home.
Since he finished the work, he went home.
After he had finished the work, he went home.
why: The participle phrase becomes a time clause with past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Choose the correct transformation: “He is too tired to continue.”
opts: He is so tired that he cannot continue.
He is very tired that he cannot continue.
He is so tired that he can continue.
He is tired so that he cannot continue.
why: 'Too ... to' becomes 'so ... that ... cannot'. GPSC-style practice item.

q: Change into a simple sentence: “He is rich and he is generous.”
why: One subject, one verb with a compound complement. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. First, she boiled water.
Q. Finally, she served the tea hot.
R. Next, she added tea leaves and milk.
S. Then she poured it into cups.
why: Order follows the cues: First, Next, Then, Finally. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. The patient took the medicine regularly.
Q. The doctor examined the patient.
R. The doctor then wrote a prescription.
S. Soon the patient recovered completely.
why: Examination, prescription, medication, recovery. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Disappointed, he returned home and called his manager.
Q. Ravi woke up late that morning.
R. At the station, he learnt that the train had already left.
S. He dressed hurriedly and hailed a taxi.
why: Chronological order: wakes, dresses, learns, returns. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. It spreads through contaminated water.
Q. Cholera is a serious bacterial disease.
R. Therefore, safe drinking water is essential for prevention.
S. Untreated, it can cause severe dehydration and even death.
why: Introduce the disease, its spread and effect, then the conclusion with 'Therefore'. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Goa soon became a major trading centre.
Q. The demand for spices grew rapidly in Europe.
R. As a result, traders sailed to India in search of them.
S. Many of them settled on the western coast.
why: Cause, result, settlement, outcome; 'them' needs an antecedent. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Hence, regular hand washing with soap is advised.
Q. Many infections spread through unwashed hands.
R. Water alone cannot remove all the germs.
S. Soap, however, breaks down their outer layer.
why: 'However' contrasts with water; 'Hence' gives the conclusion. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. However, excessive use disturbs sleep and attention.
Q. Smartphones have made communication quick and convenient.
R. Doctors therefore advise limiting screen time at night.
S. Many people now depend on them for work and study.
why: Benefits first, 'However' introduces the drawback, 'therefore' the advice. GPSC-style practice item.

q:
Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Their report, however, was rejected by the board.
Q. A team of researchers spent two years collecting data.
R. They claimed their results proved the drug’s safety.
S. The sample size, the board felt, was too small.
why: Claim, then 'however' rejection, then the reason for it. GPSC-style practice item.
